label: Redis
summary: Memory, evictions, hit ratio, connections, main-thread CPU, replication
source: redis_exporter (oliver006) metric maps, read at master on 2026-10-08 (exporter.go, info.go, slowlog.go); the queries were not run against a live exporter. redis_config_maxclients comes from CONFIG GET and is missing where CONFIG is renamed or denied. Main-thread CPU needs a server that reports used_cpu_*_main_thread. Tools' names checked the same day against Telegraf's inputs.redis (README and redis.go), Datadog's redisdb metadata.csv and constants.py, the OpenTelemetry redisreceiver documentation and the AWS/ElastiCache metric list. Datadog rates hits, misses, commands and CPU at the Agent but sends evictions and rejected connections as raw totals, so those are counters. Lifetime averages (Telegraf keyspace_hitrate, usec_per_call, latencystats percentiles) are not run-window figures and are not named. CloudWatch's Evictions, RejectedConnections and ProcessedCommands are not named: whether they count per period is unverified; nor is CacheHitRate, whose scale is unverified. ElastiCache fixes maxclients at 65,000 per node (AWS blog). INFO's per-replica lag is the seconds since that replica's last ACK, time(NULL) - repl_ack_time (server.c at unstable, checked 2026-10-09), not how far behind it is.

metrics.name: up
metrics.label: Exporter can reach Redis
metrics.description: 1 while redis_exporter can reach Redis, 0 when it cannot. Any 0 means Redis was unreachable for at least one scrape, and every other metric is blind for that span. An exporter that goes with its target (a sidecar, a deleted pod) leaves no 0, only a gap: a short gap reads PASS, and one longer than the coverage floor allows reads LOW COVERAGE.

metrics.name: memory.used.pct
metrics.label: Memory used (% of maxmemory)
metrics.description: Memory Redis uses, as a percentage of maxmemory: at 100 % it evicts keys or, under noeviction, refuses writes. It can pass 100 because buffers count too, and a node with no maxmemory has no series.

cloudwatch.note: statistic Maximum, per CacheClusterId and CacheNodeId

metrics.name: keys.evicted
metrics.label: Evicted keys per minute (peak)
metrics.description: Keys evicted to stay under maxmemory, in any minute of the run. The working set no longer fits, so misses and backend load follow.

datadog.note: a raw total since the server started, although metadata.csv calls it a gauge

metrics.name: clients.connected.pct
metrics.label: Client connections (% of maxclients)
metrics.description: Client connections as a percentage of maxclients. A steady climb at constant load usually means a client pool leak.

cloudwatch.note: ElastiCache fixes maxclients at 65,000 per node, so the scale is 100/65000; statistic Maximum, per CacheClusterId and CacheNodeId

metrics.name: clients.blocked
metrics.label: Blocked clients (peak)
metrics.description: Clients waiting on a blocking command such as BLPOP, BRPOP, BLMOVE or BZPOPMIN. A rise means consumers outnumber producers or a queue stalled. On a queue workload some blocked clients are normal.

cloudwatch.note: statistic Maximum, per CacheClusterId and CacheNodeId

metrics.name: connections.rejected
metrics.label: Rejected connections per minute (peak)
metrics.description: Connections refused because maxclients was reached, in any minute of the run. Those clients got errors.

datadog.note: a raw total since the server started, although metadata.csv calls it a gauge

metrics.name: keyspace.hit.pct
metrics.label: Keyspace hit ratio (%)
metrics.description: Read lookups that found their key, as a percentage, per minute. A drop under load means evictions, expiry, or a test reading keys it never wrote.

metrics.name: commands.rate
metrics.label: Commands processed per second (avg)
metrics.description: Commands Redis processed per second, averaged over the run: it shows the load reached Redis. A plateau while client throughput rises points at a client or pool bottleneck, a drop at a stall.

metrics.name: command.latency.avg
metrics.label: Server-side command time (avg, us)
metrics.description: Average CPU time Redis spent per command, per minute. It leaves out queueing, I/O and network, so it explains client latency rather than replacing it.

metrics.name: cpu.main.pct
metrics.label: Main-thread CPU (% of one core)
metrics.description: CPU used by the thread that runs every command, as a percentage of one core. Near 100 % Redis is saturated and every client queues, however many cores the host has.

otel.note: the sum of state=sys_main_thread and state=user_main_thread

cloudwatch.note: statistic Maximum, per CacheClusterId and CacheNodeId

metrics.name: replication.link.up
metrics.label: Replica link to primary up
metrics.description: 1 while a replica's link to its primary is up, 0 when it is down: its reads go stale and a failover may follow. Reported by replicas only.

metrics.name: replication.lag.bytes
metrics.label: Replication backlog (bytes, worst replica)
metrics.description: Bytes the primary has written that its slowest replica has not yet acknowledged. It grows when the write volume outruns replication.

datadog.note: read on the primary, one series per replica: export the max by host

metrics.name: replication.lag.seconds
metrics.label: Replication lag (s)
metrics.description: Seconds since a replica last acknowledged the primary: INFO's per-replica lag, which redis_exporter and Telegraf read on the primary. A whole-second health signal that grows when a replica stalls; CloudWatch's ReplicationLag is the replica's real time lag.

telegraf.note: read on the primary, one series per replica: export the max per server

cloudwatch.note: reported by replica nodes; statistic Maximum, per CacheClusterId and CacheNodeId

metrics.name: memory.fragmentation.ratio
metrics.label: Memory fragmentation ratio
metrics.description: Resident memory divided by the memory Redis allocated. High means memory lost to fragmentation, so the OS may kill Redis before maxmemory; below 1 means pages were swapped out, which is worse.

cloudwatch.note: statistic Maximum, per CacheClusterId and CacheNodeId

metrics.name: slowlog.entries
metrics.label: Slow commands per minute (peak)
metrics.description: Commands slower than slowlog-log-slower-than, in any minute of the run. On a single-threaded server each one stalls every other client for its whole duration.

datadog.note: new slow-log entries per second; the check reads at most 128 per run, so a burst saturates
